issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and no use of labels. The change only affects how the SLSQP polish step handles its constraints.

The candidate keeps only circle pairs whose centres start less than 0.4 apart. It then checks every pair for overlaps worse than 1e-9 and adds those pairs back, for up to 4 rounds. If overlaps remain after the 4th round, it returns those positions anyway. _polish returns only the centres, so the result stays valid if the radii are recomputed or checked afterwards, as the incumbent seems to do. If they are not, the harness's validity check would catch it as a crash, so the score can't be inflated. This is a robustness risk, not a reason to veto.

Overlaps smaller than 1e-9 are not added back to the constraint set. This only matters if the final radii are not recomputed against all pairs; a final shrink of the radii would absorb gaps that small.

Candidate -2.636 (1 run) against incumbent -2.6360 (1 run): no difference at the reported precision. With one run each there is no variance estimate, so z cannot be computed properly. Taking the difference as zero gives z = 0, which matches the harness. The change adds code and gains nothing, so 'reject' is consistent.
